usdc-0190-seattle-large-load-data-center.status_as_of_cutoff: local process / regulatory pause as of 2026-08-11. Seattle official records confirm a citywide emergency moratorium for new or expanded data centers over 20 MVA was passed as CB 121214 / Ord 127447 on 2026-06-09 and signed on 2026-06-11, with companion Resolution 32204 adopted on 2026-06-09 and signed on 2026-06-12 for impact studies. Seattle City Light's large-data-center customer class and conditions of service were passed as CB 121231 / Ord 127473 on 2026-07-21 and signed on 2026-07-22. The underlying facilities remain utility-approach/proposal-stage: official city materials report four companies approached Seattle City Light for five large-scale data centers totaling 369 MW, but no project-specific land-use approval, building permit, construction start, energization, or operating status was verified.
usdc-0190-seattle-large-load-data-center.evidence_grade: A- for Seattle Council/City Light policy actions and official 369 MW aggregate; B for developer identities, withdrawals, and remaining 249 MW active-proposal figure because those details are from local/media reporting rather than accessible official city records.

actions.result_status: Councilmembers announced emergency moratorium legislation and companion impact-study resolution after reports of four companies, five proposed large-scale data centers, and 369 MW combined maximum demand.

actions.government_body: Office of the Mayor of Seattle
actions.result_status: Mayor identified initial steps, including a one-year moratorium for new or expanded 10 MW+ large-load data centers and City Light large-load policy development.

CB 121214 passed; later Ord 127447. The ordinance adopted a moratorium on filing, accepting, processing, or approving applications for establishment, expansion, or change of use to data centers and defined covered data centers as over 20 MVA with uninterruptible power.
Resolution 32204 adopted, committing to study data-center impacts on electrical grid capacity and reliability, water, rates, land use, jobs/economy, and public health.

City Light described a proposed New Large Data Center Load Policy for new or expanded data-center electric service of 10 MVA or more, including a new rate class, cost-based rates, customer cost responsibility, service queue, and demand-response requirements.

CB 121231 passed; later Ord 127473. The ordinance established new retail rate schedules, a new customer class, and conditions of service for data centers whose electricity demand constitutes a new large load.

actions.access_caveat: RRDA news gives a month-level transfer date and 619-acre figure; the SBOA-filed audit gives 623.20 acres by Blocke, LLC but does not name Meta in the same line.

actions.exact_result_status: IEDC announced Meta's nearly 700,000-square-foot River Ridge facility, construction starting that month, expected 2026 operations, and a 35-year data-center sales-tax exemption for at least $800 million of eligible capital; city and River Ridge incentives were described but not itemized in a vote record.
actions.access_caveat: Official state announcement accessible; it does not link the Clark County/Jeffersonville approval packet or a building permit.

actions.exact_result_status: City announcement described an $800 million, 619-acre campus at River Ridge Commerce Center with a nearly 700,000-square-foot facility, more than 1,200 peak construction jobs, 100 tech jobs, and renewable-energy support.
actions.access_caveat: City news item confirms site scale and location but is not a permit or site-plan packet.

actions.action_type: annual planning report / construction status evidence
actions.exact_result_status: The 2024 Planning and Zoning annual report identified the groundbreaking of Meta's data center at River Ridge as one of the year's largest projects, supporting classification as site work-construction rather than merely announced.
actions.access_caveat: Official annual report confirms groundbreaking but does not include building permit numbers or electrical capacity.

usdc-0162-nscale-ionic-digital-ward-coun.status_as_of_cutoff: energized: Texas Comptroller now lists Cedarvale, Barslow/Pyote TX Data Center as a Registered Qualifying Large Data Center Project effective 2026-03-16 with Ionic Digital Cedarvale LLC as owner, Nscale Ward County Borrower SPV, LLC as occupant, and Nscale Ward County, LLC / Ionic Digital Mining, LLC operator registrations. Ionic's SEC S-1 filed 2026-06-29 says the Ward County property is fully energized at 234 MW as of 2026-03-31, Nscale leases 234 MW under a 126-month agreement, monthly fixed lease payments commence 2026-08, and AI campus use begins in Q3 2026. actions.result_or_status: The same Comptroller registry row lists 2026-03-15 as the exemption end date; no replacement or extension row was located in the retrieved list.

actions.notes: Tax-incentive status; not evidence of project cancellation.

actions.result_or_status: Ionic announced a lease agreement with Nscale for the Cedarvale facility in Barstow, Texas; Nscale would lease the full 234 MW capacity under a 10-year triple-net lease with approximately $2 billion in contracted revenues.
actions.access_caveat: Company announcement; not a county permit or construction approval.
actions.notes: Supports owner/developer identity, 234 MW capacity, lease structure, and AI/HPC reuse of the Cedarvale facility.

actions.result_or_status: Nscale announced an expanded Microsoft deal including approximately 104,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs in a roughly 240 MW Texas hyperscale AI campus leased from Ionic Digital, with phased NVIDIA AI infrastructure services to Microsoft from Q3 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Nscale rounds the Texas campus to roughly 240 MW, while Ionic/SEC lease materials state 234 MW.
actions.notes: Also states an intended 1.2 GW footprint over time and Microsoft option on a second 700 MW phase starting in late 2027.

actions.body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Ionic Digital Inc.
actions.result_or_status: SEC-filed net lease identifies Ionic Digital Cedarvale LLC as landlord and Nscale Ward County LLC as tenant, effective 2025-10-14 and amended 2026-02-27; Exhibit A describes the leased premises as 50.079 acres in Ward County.
actions.access_caveat: Filed contract confirms parties and premises but redacts rent rates and is not a local land-use approval.
actions.notes: Lease references the existing qualified data center exemption and Nscale/Nscale SPV intent to apply as qualified operator/occupant.

actions.result_or_status: Comptroller current list records Cedarvale, Barslow/Pyote TX Data Center as a Registered Qualifying Large Data Center Project effective 2026-03-16, with Ionic Digital Cedarvale LLC owner registration LD449964-OW1, Nscale Ward County Borrower SPV, LLC occupant registration LD449964-OC1, and operator registrations for Nscale Ward County, LLC and Ionic Digital Mining, LLC.
actions.access_caveat: State tax-incentive/registration record, not a county construction permit.
actions.notes: This appears to supersede or follow the prior DC961705/DC737649 row that ended 2026-03-15.

actions.body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Ionic Digital Inc.
actions.result_or_status: Ionic's S-1 states its largest facility is in Ward County, Texas; as of 2026-03-31 the self-owned, recently constructed property was fully energized at 234 MW, with 50 of 136 acres developed and the remaining 86 acres being developed to support up to approximately 700 MW. It also states Nscale contracted for 234 MW under a 126-month lease, monthly fixed payments commence in 2026-08, Nscale is obligated to lease an additional 89 MW if available, and expansion is subject to regulatory approval.
actions.access_caveat: Issuer disclosure; forward-looking expansion language is not proof that 89 MW/700 MW/1.2 GW has been energized.
actions.notes: Supports status layer as energized for current 234 MW, while AI service delivery is still described as a Q3 2026 ramp.

capacity_detail.notes: Use 234 MW as verified current capacity. Nscale rounds the initial Texas campus to roughly 240 MW; 89 MW, 700 MW, and 1.2 GW are contingent/planned expansion figures.

usdc-0056-harwood-3b-ai-factory.status_as_of_cutoff: site work-construction as of 2026-08-11. The original local lead is now resolved to Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 2 campus near Harwood. Applied Digital announced the $3 billion project on 2025-08-18, later described it as currently under construction, and reported on 2026-04-08 that both Harwood buildings were progressing with foundations largely complete and precast erection/MEP mobilization underway. North Dakota PSC Case No. PU-26-22 separately approved the Agassiz 345-kV transmission line and substation on 2026-04-29, and a 2026-05-05 PSC filing noticed intent to start construction of that power project on or shortly after 2026-05-18. No source reviewed confirms energization, ready-for-service, partial live, or full buildout for Polaris Forge 2.
usdc-0056-harwood-3b-ai-factory.evidence_grade: high for project identity, owner/developer, under-construction status, 200 MW critical IT lease, 280 MW announced/gross planning capacity, and PSC-approved supporting power infrastructure; medium for exact parcel/address because public sources describe the area but do not publish a definitive parcel list in the reviewed record.

actions.result_status: Applied Digital announced Polaris Forge 2, a $3 billion AI Factory near Harwood, North Dakota, designed for 280 MW with initial operations planned in 2026 and full capacity in early 2027; the announcement said power was secured through Cass County Electric Cooperative and more than 900 acres had been contracted.

usdc-0056-harwood-3b-ai-factory.capacity_note: capacity_mw records currently contracted critical IT load. Applied Digital's 2025 project announcement used 280 MW for the Harwood AI Factory; later lease, financing, and quarterly updates consistently identify 200 MW of critical IT load at Polaris Forge 2. PSC and media references also cite up to 280 MW large-load/gross power demand. Treat 200 MW as critical IT and 280 MW as announced/gross utility-load planning capacity unless later filings reconcile the measures.

contradictions.resolution: Use 200 MW for capacity_mw as critical IT load and preserve 280 MW as announced/gross planning capacity in capacity_note.
